text:
Vegas is 12-5-2, on top of a road trip that keeps producing wins, and the reason is the same one it usually is with this franchise: the goaltending is bailing out an ordinary week. The Golden Knights have won three straight, 9-4, but took only 49% of the expected goals in those games, with their goalies saving 6.2 goals more than expected. Sunday in Buffalo was the clearest case: outshot early, out-attempted 78-51, and Adin Hill made it a 4-1 win.

Over the full season the process is better than that. Vegas takes about 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and two units carry it. Jack Eichel, Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev have outscored teams 10-4, and Shea Theodore with Brayden McNabb is 19-8 in goals over 283 minutes, one of the best pairs we track. Mitch Marner's line with William Karlsson and Brett Howden is breaking even.

The soft spots are lower in the lineup. Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon have 36% of the chances together, and the Nic Dowd line is at 29%. Trevor Connelly's late winner in Detroit has SinBin.vegas arguing for a bigger role, and we'd be curious to see it. In net, Hill and Carter Hart are splitting the work, and both have had good nights this trip. Our simulations make Vegas a 96% playoff team projecting about 105 points.
